title: Biotechnology in India
wikitext:
{{Short description|Biotechnology industry in India}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2022}}
'''Biotechnology in India''' is a [[Sunrise industry|sunrise sector]] within the [[Economy of India|Indian economy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Livemint |date=2022-06-11 |title=India's biotech sector likely to reach $150 billion in 4 years: Minister |url=https://www.livemint.com/industry/manufacturing/indias-biotech-sector-likely-to-reach-150-billion-in-4-years-minister-11654957252869.html |access-date=2022-12-06 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref> Agencies of the [[Government of India]] concerned with the [[biotechnology]] industry include the [[Department of Biotechnology]] and the proposed [[Biotechnology Regulatory Authority of India]]. As of 2022, the sector is valued at $80 billion.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Basu |first=Mohana |date=2022-07-20 |title=R&D investment in Indian biotech tripled in 2021 to cross $1 billion, says govt report |url=https://theprint.in/economy/rd-investment-in-indian-biotech-tripled-in-2021-to-cross-1-billion-says-govt-report/1047304/ |access-date=2022-12-25 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}}</ref> Biotechnology in India is in a growth phase and the sector is expected to be valued at $150 billion by 2025 and surpass $300 billion in value by 2030.<ref name=":2" />

== History ==
The first Indian [[biotechnology]] company to be established was [[Biocon]], which was founded by [[Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw]] in 1978.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dey |first=Soma |date=2019 |title=Biocon: Taking a Crack at the Global Biosimilar Market |journal=South Asian Journal of Business and Management Cases |volume=8 |issue=1 |pages=100–110 |doi=10.1177/2277977918803186 |issn=2277-9779|doi-access=free }}</ref> The Indian biotechnology industry formally began in 1986 with the establishment of the [[Department of Biotechnology]] (DBT) by the [[Ministry of Science and Technology (India)|Ministry of Science and Technology]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Nogrady |first=Bianca |date=2018-12-12 |title=How Indian biotech is driving innovation |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=564 |issue=7735 |pages=S53–S55 |doi=10.1038/d41586-018-07671-9|pmid=30542184 |doi-access=free }}</ref> 1999 saw the founding of [[Genome Valley]], an Indian [[high-technology]] business district spread across {{convert|2000|acre|km2|adj=on}}/(3.1 sq mi) in [[Hyderabad]], [[Telangana]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/pharma-majors-queue-up-for-space-at-hyderabads-genome-valley/articleshow/77341405.cms|title=Pharma majors queue up for space at Hyderabad's Genome Valley|website=[[The Times of India]] |date=4 August 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Special Correspondent |url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/article2648392.ece?css=print |title=Today's Paper / NATIONAL : BioAsia-2012 to focus on vaccines, IPR, CROs and investments |newspaper=The Hindu |date=2011-11-22 |accessdate=2012-08-21}}</ref> Also from 1999, [[St. Joseph's College, Irinjalakuda|St. Joseph’s College, Irinjalakuda]], Kerala is offering a government-aided B.Sc. Biotechnology program. It is the only institution in Kerala offering an aided graduation program in biotechnology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Department of Biotechnology, St. Joseph's College, Irinjalakuda |url=https://stjosephs.edu.in/department/biotechnology/content/home.html}}</ref> In 2024, the Indian government approved the {{INRConvert|9197|c|year=2024|to=USD}} Bio-RIDE scheme to focus on three areas of biotechnology in India: [[research and development]], entrepreneurship and industrial development, and [[biomanufacturing]] and biofoundries, with the goal of growing India's [[bioeconomy]] to $300 billion by 2030.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=18 September 2024 |title=Govt greenlights ₹9,197 crore Bio-RIDE scheme to advance biotechnology, biomanufacturing |url=https://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/renewable/govt-greenlights-9197-crore-bio-ride-scheme-to-advance-biotechnology-biomanufacturing/113458237 |access-date=19 May 2025 |website=ET EnergyWorld}}</ref> 

== Regulation ==

=== Department of Biotechnology ===
{{main|Department of Biotechnology}}
The Department of Biotechnology is an [[Government of India|Indian government]] department under the [[Ministry of Science and Technology (India)|Ministry of Science and Technology]], responsible for administering development and commercialization in the field of modern [[biology]] and biotechnology in India. The DBT was also one of the world's first government departments that was established to focus solely on the biotechnology sector.<ref name=":1" />

=== Biotechnology Regulatory Authority of India ===
{{main|Biotechnology Regulatory Authority of India}}
The Biotechnology Regulatory Authority of India (BRAI) is a proposed regulatory body in India for uses of biotechnology products including [[genetically modified organism]]s (GMOs).<ref>{{citation|title=Regulatory Authority to be Set Up on Bio-Technology|url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=84347|publisher=[[Press Information Bureau|PIB]], [[Government of India|GOI]]|date=22 May 2012}}</ref> The institute was first suggested under the Biotechnology Regulatory Authority of India (BRAI) draft bill prepared by the [[Department of Biotechnology]] in 2008. Since then, it has undergone several revisions.<ref>{{citation|title=BRAI Bill leaves biotech commercialisation in limbo|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/brai-bill-leaves-biotech-commercialisation-in-limbo/article621692.ece|newspaper=[[The Hindu]]|date=9 September 2010}}</ref>

==Companies==

=== Biologics and biosimilars manufactures ===
Several of the large Indian pharmaceutical companies also manufacture [[Biopharmaceutical|biologics]] and [[Biosimilar|biosimilars]]. One of Biocon's subsidiaries, Biocon Biologics, manufactures [[Biosimilar|biosimilars]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Who we are - Biocon - Global Biopharmaceutical company |url=https://www.biocon.com/about-us/who-we-are/ |access-date=2022-09-11 |website=Biocon |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Kumar |first=Manoj |date=2023-05-24 |title=India's Biocon Biologics says biosimilars put revenue on $1 bln trajectory |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/indias-biocon-biologics-says-biosimilars-put-revenue-1-bln-trajectory-2023-05-24/ |access-date=2023-08-08}}</ref> [[Intas Pharmaceuticals]] also manufactures biosimilars.<ref>{{Cite web |last=BS Reporter |date=23 February 2015 |title=Ahmedabad-based Intas Pharma launches biosimilar in EU |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/ahmedabad-based-intas-pharma-launches-biosimilar-in-eu-115022300721_1.html |access-date=17 August 2023 |website=Business Standard}}</ref> [[Dr. Reddy's Laboratories]] entered the biosimilars market in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 March 2012 |title=Dr Reddy’s looks to biosimilars for growth |url=https://www.gabionline.net/biosimilars/news/Dr-Reddy-s-looks-to-biosimilars-for-growth |access-date=2023-08-21 |website=Generics and Biosimilars Initiative |language=en}}</ref> [[Cipla]] entered the biosimilars market in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 July 2010 |title=Cipla enters the biosimilars market |url=https://gabionline.net/biosimilars/news/Cipla-enters-the-biosimilars-market |access-date=2023-08-21 |website=Generics and Biosimilars Initiative |language=en}}</ref> [[Aurobindo Pharma]] is focusing on developing biosimilars in various segments.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Neetu Chandra |date=2022-09-13 |title=Biosimilars has Pushed Aurobindo Pharma to Second Place Among Indian Pharma Companies. Can it Become No. 1? |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/corporate/story/biosimilars-has-pushed-aurobindo-pharma-to-second-place-among-indian-pharma-companies-can-it-become-no-1-347117-2022-09-13 |access-date=2023-08-10 |website=Business Today |language=en}}</ref> Enzene Biosciences is the biologics subsidiary of [[Alkem Laboratories]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 June 2023 |title=Alkem launches first cetuximab similar biologic in India |url=https://gabionline.net/biosimilars/news/alkem-launches-first-cetuximab-similar-biologic-in-india |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=Generics and Biosimilars Initiative |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Roy |first=Shubhobrota Dev |date=2023-01-30 |title=Enzene snags $50 mn from parent firm, others |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/start-ups/enzene-snags-50-mn-from-parent-firm-others-11675005919716.html |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=Mint |language=en}}</ref>

Reliance Life Sciences, owned by [[Mukesh Ambani]], Asia's wealthiest man, manufactures biosimilars and other biopharmaceutical and [[Medication|pharmaceutical]] products.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gopalan |first=Krishna |date=2023-07-31 |title=Reliance Life Sciences: How a new campus in Nashik is helping the firm make the moves |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/industry/pharma/story/reliance-life-sciences-how-a-new-campus-in-nashik-is-helping-the-firm-make-the-moves-392020-2023-07-31 |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=Business Today |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mukesh Ambani |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/mukesh-ambani/ |access-date=2023-01-27 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>      

=== Vaccine manufactures ===
India is the world's largest [[vaccine]] maker as of 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Roy |first1=Abhirup |last2=Rocha |first2=Euan |last3=Das |first3=Krishna N. |date=2020-12-10 |title=Not without India: World's pharmacy gears up for vaccine race |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-india-vaccine-idUSKBN28K10E |access-date=2022-12-26}}</ref> Indian vaccine manufactures include the [[Serum Institute of India]] (SII).<ref>{{Cite web |title=About Serum Institute Of India Pvt. Ltd. |url=https://www.seruminstitute.com/about_us.php |access-date=2022-09-06 |website=www.seruminstitute.com}}</ref> SII is the world's largest vaccine manufacturer.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kalra |first=Aditya |date=2022-05-24 |title=Indian vaccine giant Serum plans African plant in global expansion |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/indian-vaccine-giant-serum-plans-african-plant-global-expansion-2022-05-23/ |access-date=2022-09-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Robertson |first=Chiyo |date=2021-02-28 |title=Covid: How this Indian firm is vaccinating the world |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-56218058 |access-date=2022-09-06}}</ref> Reliance Life Sciences, among other products, also manufactures vaccines.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bl Bengaluru Bureau |date=2023-08-21 |title=ABB India to automate Reliance Life Sciences’ biopharmaceutical facilities |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/abb-india-to-automate-reliance-life-sciences-biopharmaceutical-facilities/article67218856.ece |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=The Hindu Business Line |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Priyanka |date=2022-11-02 |title=ICMR picks 6 firms for monkeypox vaccines |url=https://www.livemint.com/science/health/icmr-picks-6-firms-for-monkeypox-vaccines-11667323425250.html |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=Mint |language=en}}</ref> Another established vaccine manufacturer is [[Bharat Biotech]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bharat Biotech International Ltd - Company Profile and News |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/company/7535940Z:IN |access-date=2022-09-06 |website=Bloomberg.com |language=en}}</ref> [[Hester Biosciences]] is Asia’s largest company that manufactures [[Animal vaccination|animal and poultry vaccines]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://www.hester.in/about |access-date=2022-10-06 |website=www.hester.in}}</ref>

|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/syngene-to-acquire-unit-3s-biologics-facility/articleshow/101529416.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-08-07 |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> Laurus Bio is a subsidiary of [[Laurus Labs]] and was originally an independent company named Richcore, before Laurus Labs acquired Richcore and renamed it.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Ramarathinam |first=Ashwin |date=2020-11-25 |title=Laurus Labs buys 73% stake in Biotech firm Richcore Lifesciences for Rs247 crore |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/laurus-labs-buys-73-stake-in-biotech-firm-richcore-lifesciences-for-rs247-crore-11606311893776.html |access-date=2022-05-02 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Laurus Bio {{!}} Enabling precision fermentation and synthetic biology |url=https://laurus.bio/about-us/ |access-date=2022-05-02 |website=LAURUS Bio |language=en-US}}</ref> Laurus Bio, among other products and services, also offers CDMO services for [[Microorganism|microbial]] [[Industrial fermentation|precision fermentation]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CDMO Services |url=https://laurus.bio/cdmo-services/#1620724132047-ad99010b-d1a6 |access-date=22 August 2023 |website=Laurus Bio}}</ref> In 2021, Cipla entered into a [[joint venture]] with biopharmaceutical CDMO company Kemwell Biopharma, to develop, manufacture and commercialize biosimilars for global markets.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 August 2021 |title=Cipla, Kemwell Enter Biosimilars |url=https://www.concordbiotech.com/contract-research-manufacturing |access-date=2023-08-30 |website=Concord Biotech}}</ref>

=== Active pharmaceutical ingredients ===
Concord Biotech manufactures, among other products, fermentation based complex [[Active ingredient|active pharmaceutical ingredients]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=About us |url=https://www.concordbiotech.com/about-overview |access-date=2023-08-04 |website=Concord Biotech}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Manohar |first=Asit |date=2023-08-05 |title=Concord Biotech IPO: What GMP, subscription signal as offer ends on Tuesday |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/ipo/concord-biotech-ipo-what-gmp-subscription-status-signal-as-offer-ends-on-tuesday-11691224927205.html |access-date=2023-08-30 |website=Mint |language=en}}</ref>

=== Bioinformatics ===
[[Tata Consultancy Services]] (TCS), one of the largest [[information technology]] companies in India, offers [[bioinformatics]] and [[biostatistics]] services.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TCS’ cutting-edge Genomics Research Services |url=https://www.tcs.com/what-we-do/industries/life-sciences/solution/cutting-edge-genomics-research |access-date=2023-09-06 |website=TATA Consultancy Services |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Reymond |first=Emilie |date=2007-09-04 |title=Tata bags major BPO deal with Roche |url=https://www.outsourcing-pharma.com/Article/2007/09/05/Tata-bags-major-BPO-deal-with-Roche |access-date=2023-09-25 |website=Outsourcing-Pharma |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Other established companies ===
* Advanced Enzymes<ref>{{Cite web |title=Corporate Profile |url=https://www.advancedenzymes.com/corporate-profile/ |access-date=2022-10-06 |website=Advanced Enzymes |language=en-US}}</ref> 
* [[Sea6 Energy]] is a startup working for producing fuel from [[seaweed]].<ref>{{citation |title=How Bengaluru became the biotech capital of India |date=12 November 2015 |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/healthcare/how-bengaluru-became-the-biotech-capital-of-india/articleshow/49751173.cms |publisher=[[The Economic Times]]}}</ref>

=== Startups ===
There have been an increasing number of [[Startup company|startups]] being founded in the Indian biotechnology industry. In 2021, the total number of biotechnology startups stood at 5365, whereas in 2010, there were only 50 startups in the sector.<ref name=":2" /> As of 2021, more than half of the biotechnology startups are being founded in the medical sector, however, other large sectors where biotechnology startups are being founded include 18% in the biotechnology services sector and 14% of startups are in agricultural biotechnology.<ref name=":1" />  

== Biotechnology parks ==
The DBT has set up biotechnology [[Business park|parks]] in India, and as of 2022, there are 9 biotechnology parks across the country.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=PTI |date=28 May 2022 |title=North India's first biotech park inaugurated in J-K's Kathua |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/india/north-indias-first-biotech-park-inaugurated-in-j-ks-kathua/articleshow/91858934.cms |access-date=2022-12-28}}</ref> The parks have been set up by the DBT to give infrastructure support that will assist in making biotechnology research into products and services.<ref name=":3" /> The biotechnology parks give scientists and [[small and medium-sized enterprises]] facilities that can help them in developing and demonstrating technologies, and assist in their pilot plant studies as well.
